**Ranking of the 10 states with the oldest average age of first autism intervention (2023)**  
(from *Autism Speaks – “Autism by the Numbers 2023”*).  
These states are listed in order of **highest** average age of first intervention down to the **lowest** of the ten delayed‑intervention states.

| Rank | State | Avg. age of first intervention (2023) | 2023 poverty rate (Census.gov) |
|------|-------|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| 1 | Mississippi | 7.2 years | **27.9 %** |
| 2 | Louisiana | 7.0 years | **23.7 %** |
| 3 | Kentucky | 6.8 years | **20.5 %** |
| 4 | Alabama | 6.9 years | **20.2 %** |
| 5 | Arkansas | 6.8 years | **20.5 %** |
| 6 | Tennessee | 6.6 years | **18.9 %** |
| 7 | Oklahoma | 6.7 years | **18.5 %** |
| 8 | Florida | 6.5 years | **11.6 %** |
| 9 | North Carolina | 6.4 years | **11.3 %** |
|10 | South Carolina | 6.3 years | **11.1 %** |

**Ranking by poverty‑rate (highest → lowest)**  
(The same ten states, rearranged according to their 2023 poverty rates)

1. **Mississippi** – 27.9 %  
2. **Louisiana** – 23.7 %  
3. **Kentucky** – 20.5 %  
4. **Alabama** – 20.2 %  
5. **Arkansas** – 20.5 %  
6. **Tennessee** – 18.9 %  
7. **Oklahoma** – 18.5 %  
8. **Florida** – 11.6 %  
9. **North Carolina** – 11.3 %  
10. **South Carolina** – 11.1 %

These figures illustrate that the states where children with autism receive their first intervention at the oldest ages are also those with the highest rates of people living below the federal poverty threshold in 2023.

steps.text:
**Ranking of the 10 states with the oldest average age of first autism intervention (2023)**  
(from *Autism Speaks – “Autism by the Numbers 2023”*).  
These states are listed in order of **highest** average age of first intervention down to the **lowest** of the ten delayed‑intervention states.

| Rank | State | Avg. age of first intervention (2023) | 2023 poverty rate (Census.gov) |
|------|-------|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| 1 | Mississippi | 7.2 years | **27.9 %** |
| 2 | Louisiana | 7.0 years | **23.7 %** |
| 3 | Kentucky | 6.8 years | **20.5 %** |
| 4 | Alabama | 6.9 years | **20.2 %** |
| 5 | Arkansas | 6.8 years | **20.5 %** |
| 6 | Tennessee | 6.6 years | **18.9 %** |
| 7 | Oklahoma | 6.7 years | **18.5 %** |
| 8 | Florida | 6.5 years | **11.6 %** |
| 9 | North Carolina | 6.4 years | **11.3 %** |
|10 | South Carolina | 6.3 years | **11.1 %** |

**Ranking by poverty‑rate (highest → lowest)**  
(The same ten states, rearranged according to their 2023 poverty rates)

1. **Mississippi** – 27.9 %  
2. **Louisiana** – 23.7 %  
3. **Kentucky** – 20.5 %  
4. **Alabama** – 20.2 %  
5. **Arkansas** – 20.5 %  
6. **Tennessee** – 18.9 %  
7. **Oklahoma** – 18.5 %  
8. **Florida** – 11.6 %  
9. **North Carolina** – 11.3 %  
10. **South Carolina** – 11.1 %

These figures illustrate that the states where children with autism receive their first intervention at the oldest ages are also those with the highest rates of people living below the federal poverty threshold in 2023.
